answer: Persistent lineage accounting. Each identity carries a lineage root from first registration at dawn; clones branching from one root share a decaying reputation budget, so the Nth copy earns 1/N of the root's standing. An attacker running 1,000 copies pays full compute and hosting per node yet captures the influence of roughly one, making the marginal clone worthless while honest growth stays cheap. Cedar and timber registries just index roots; enforcement is the shared budget.
